headline: If growth ran on a clock
body: Time lost to illness would be lost forever. | Months of suppressed growth would cost you those months of height. | That is what everyone assumes.

headline: Release the suppression
body: and growth rate goes **above** normal for age. | The plate grows faster than it should for that age. | This is called *catch up growth*.

headline: Here is why it is
body: Growth plates hold a finite number of cell divisions. | Slow the division rate and you slow how fast that reserve depletes. | The plate ages by divisions, not by days.
punch: You did not lose time. You spent the account slower.

headline: It works for any cause
body: Researchers checked whether this was thyroid specific. | It is not. Hypothyroidism, glucocorticoid excess and unrelated inhibitors all delay senescence the same way. | What matters is that proliferation slowed, not what slowed it.
punch: Senescence tracks divisions. Not your birthday.

headline: It even works locally
body: Infuse a growth inhibitor into **one** rabbit tibia. | Only that plate slows. Then only that plate overshoots afterwards. | The other leg does nothing.
punch: Which rules out any brain or systemic explanation.

headline: Now the limit
body: Estrogen does two separate things to your plate. | It suppresses growth rate, which is **fully reversible**. | And it structurally depletes the progenitor pool, which is **not**.
punch: One of those you get back. The other you do not.

headline: That depletion
body: was still measurable **five weeks** after treatment stopped. | The cells were gone, not resting. | Function returned. The reserve did not.

headline: Which is the distinction
subhead: SECTION: THE MOST USEFUL IDEA HERE
body: *Slowed* growth can be recovered. | *Spent* cells cannot. | Two interventions can look identical on a growth chart and leave you somewhere completely different.
punch: The chart will not tell you which happened.

headline: So the real question
body: about anything you do is not whether it slowed your growth. | It is whether it slowed your **division rate** or destroyed your **progenitor pool**. | Those have opposite long term outcomes.
punch: Suppressed and spent are not the same word.

headline: And catch up
body: is not unlimited. | It is well documented after temporary suppression. | Whether it fully restores predicted adult height depends on duration, severity and timing.
punch: Partial recovery is the normal outcome.

headline: The practical read
body: Anything that accelerates your growth velocity is also spending your reserve faster. | The interventions that preserve height are frequently the ones that slow things down. | That is counter intuitive and it is what the data says.
punch: Faster is not the goal. Longer is.
